editorial:
Imagine eight young filmmakers locked in a single hotel room for one night with a very weird set of rules. They each have to make a tiny movie under three minutes long, and every single story has to include the exact phrase, I miss Sonja Henie. It feels less like a standard movie and more like a strange art project or a game of telephone. You get this wild mix of different styles and ideas all happening in the same attic space, making the whole experience feel like a fever dream that moves quickly from one odd scene to the next.

What really works here is how the different moods clash. Some parts are funny, while others are just plain confusing, but that is the point. Since it was shot in one night, you can tell the creators were just having fun and pushing boundaries. If you like movies that break all the rules, you will love this. It is a short ride, so it is perfect for a quick watch. You can try hunting for a digital copy to rent on Apple TV or just add the physical disc to your collection if you can find a rare copy for your shelf.
endingExplained: Since this is a collection of short sketches rather than one long story, there is no traditional plot twist. The film wraps up as the final director finishes their short piece. The whole point is the repetition of that one weird line about the figure skater. It ends by showing you that art can be made from simple constraints, leaving you to wonder why that specific sentence was chosen in the first place.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves strange art films and indie experiments.
